verdicts.claim: Automatic checkpointing starts when a COMMIT takes the WAL to 1000 pages or more (about 4 MB). From then on, each COMMIT runs a PASSIVE
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'grow the WAL until the WAL becomes about 1000 pages in size, then to run a checkpoint operation for each subsequent COMMIT until the WAL is reset to be smaller than 1000 pages'; 'automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE'; SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT named.

verdicts.claim: SQLite says the bug is likely present in 3.7.0 through 3.51.2. It is fixed in 3.51.3 (released 2026-03-13) and later, and backported to 3.44.6 and 3.50.7
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'likely present in all version of SQLite from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 ... fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) ... Backports ... 3.44.6 and 3.50.7'; release log: 'Fix the WAL-reset database corruption bug'.

verdicts.claim: The WAL-reset bug ... needs two or more connections, in separate threads or processes, that write or checkpoint at the same instant
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'two or more database connections open on the same file, in separate threads or processes, and when those two connections attempt to write or checkpoint at the same instant'.

verdicts.claim: Every checkpoint call takes an exclusive checkpoint lock ... returns SQLITE_BUSY at once and the busy handler is not invoked. FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE ... finish as PASSIVE
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'All calls obtain an exclusive "checkpoint" lock ... SQLITE_BUSY is returned. Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked'; 'proceeds ... in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE'.

verdicts.claim: Only PASSIVE runs for sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and for automatic checkpoints. FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE need sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2()
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'All checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE. FULL and RESTART checkpoints ... can only be initiated by a call to sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2()'.

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint returns one row with three integers. Column 1 is 1 when the equivalent sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() call would return SQLITE_BUSY
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'returns a single row with three integer columns ... 1 if the equivalent call would have returned SQLITE_BUSY. The second column is the number of modified pages that have been written to the write-ahead log file'.

verdicts.claim: Only a TRUNCATE checkpoint or the journal_size_limit pragma (default -1, no limit) truncates it
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'the write-ahead log file is not truncated following a checkpoint'; 'The default journal size limit is -1 (no limit)'.

verdicts.claim: Litestream v0.5.x ... truncate-page-n defaults to 121359 pages (about 500 MB) ... min-checkpoint-page-count defaults to 1000 ... checkpoint-interval 1 minute
verdicts.evidence: Guide: 'truncate-page-n: 121359 # Default: ~500MB ... Attempts a PASSIVE checkpoint first, then falls back to a TRUNCATE'; 'min-checkpoint-page-count: 1000 # Default: ~4MB'; 'checkpoint-interval: 1m # Default: 1 minute'; 'Only runs if WAL has at least 1 page'. (Claim was marked Tentative but sampled as load-bearing numbers; v0.5.x version label not checked.)

verdicts.claim: Litestream ... holds a long-running read transaction so no other process can reset the WAL, reads new WAL pages itself, and calls sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2()
verdicts.evidence: how-it-works: 'starts a long-running read transaction to prevent any other process from checkpointing and restarting the WAL file ... manually calls out to SQLite to perform checkpoints'; guide names sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2().

verdicts.claim: Since SQLite 3.11.0 (2016-02-15), a transaction writes each changed page to the WAL once, so the WAL is proportional to the transaction size
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'As of SQLite version 3.11.0 (2016-02-15), the WAL file for a single transaction should be proportional in size to the transaction itself. Pages ... should only be written into the WAL file once'. (Claim marked Tentative; sampled for the version/date.)

notes: All 7 cited sources were cache hits with text; 0 web fetches used.

Two sampled claims (Litestream thresholds, 3.11.0 proportional WAL) carry 'Tentative:' prefixes; sampled anyway because few untentative numeric claims remained. Both are fully supported by cached text and could drop the Tentative label.
